content: Morning sickness refers to nausea and vomiting that can occur at any time of the day during pregnancy, despite its name suggesting it only happens in the morning. Symptoms of Morning Sickness: Morning sickness is a very common condition during pregnancy. Most pregnant women experience some degree of nausea, and approximately one-third of them also experience vomiting. Symptoms typically begin during the first month of pregnancy and often persist until the 14th to 16th week (around the third or fourth month). However, some women may experience nausea and vomiting throughout their entire pregnancy. Morning sickness does not harm the baby unless it leads to significant weight loss, such as in cases of severe vomiting. The severity of morning sickness in one pregnancy does not predict how it will manifest in future pregnancies. Causes of Morning Sickness: The exact cause of morning sickness remains unknown. It is believed to be associated with hormonal changes or low blood sugar levels during early pregnancy. Factors such as emotional stress, fatigue, traveling, or certain foods can exacerbate the condition. Nausea tends to be more common and severe in pregnancies involving twins or triplets. When to Seek Urgent Medical Care: Contact your doctor if: Morning sickness does not improve despite trying home remedies. Nausea and vomiting persist beyond the fourth month of pregnancy. While this can be normal for some women, it should still be evaluated. You lose more than 2 pounds. You vomit blood or material resembling coffee grounds (seek immediate medical attention in this case). You vomit more than three times a day or are unable to keep food or liquids down. Diagnosis: Your doctor will perform a physical examination, including a pelvic exam, and assess for signs of dehydration. They may ask questions such as: Are you experiencing only nausea, or are you also vomiting? Does the nausea and vomiting occur daily? Does it last throughout the day? Are you able to keep any food or fluids down? Have you been traveling recently? Has your schedule changed? Are you feeling stressed? What foods have you been eating? Do you smoke? What have you tried to alleviate your symptoms? Are you experiencing any other symptoms, such as headaches, abdominal pain, breast tenderness, dry mouth, excessive thirst, or unintended weight loss? Diagnostic tests may include: Blood tests, such as a complete blood count (CBC) and blood chemistry. Urine tests. Ultrasound imaging. Home Care Recommendations: Maintain a positive attitude, as morning sickness typically resolves after the first three to four months of pregnancy. To reduce nausea: Eat a few soda crackers or dry toast upon waking, even before getting out of bed. Have a small snack at bedtime and when waking up to use the bathroom at night. Avoid large meals; instead, snack every 1–2 hours throughout the day and stay hydrated. Consume foods high in protein and complex carbohydrates, such as peanut butter on apple slices or celery, nuts, cheese, crackers, milk, cottage cheese, and yogurt. Avoid foods high in fat and salt but low in nutritional value. Use ginger products, such as ginger tea, ginger candy, or ginger soda, as they have been proven effective against morning sickness. Additional tips: Consider acupressure wristbands or acupuncture. If opting for acupuncture, consult your doctor and choose a practitioner experienced in treating pregnant women. Avoid smoking and exposure to secondhand smoke. Avoid taking medications for morning sickness unless prescribed by a doctor. Ensure proper ventilation in rooms to minimize odors. When feeling nauseated, bland foods like gelatin, broth, ginger ale, and saltine crackers can help soothe the stomach. Take prenatal vitamins at night. Increase vitamin B6 intake through foods like whole grains, nuts, seeds, peas, and beans (legumes). Consult your doctor about taking vitamin B6 supplements. Where to Find Medical Care for Morning Sickness: Consult your healthcare provider or a specialist in maternal-fetal medicine for further evaluation and management of morning sickness.
